name: Charnel Propulsion
sovereign_territory: A heavily fortified industrial campus straddling the former Indiana-Michigan border called the Ossuary, built over a decommissioned automotive manufacturing megasite; includes two private launch corridors and a restricted airspace zone extending 40 kilometers
founding_story: Charnel Propulsion emerged in 2138 from the ruins of three bankrupt aerospace contractors whose combined intellectual property was purchased at liquidation auction by GLMZ venture bloc Greyfield Partners. The new entity was handed to engineer-director Oskar Brennthal, a Hungarian-born propulsion specialist who had previously been blacklisted from government contracts for testing an unlicensed plasma drive over Lake Erie. Brennthal stripped the legacy companies down to their best patents and built Charnel around a single obsession: post-chemical propulsion for atmospheric and near-orbital use.
security_force: Pyre Division — 5,800 personnel combining conventional base security with an aerial interdiction wing operating six prototype VTOL gunships. Pyre Division is authorized for lethal force by default within Ossuary airspace and has shot down seventeen unauthorized drones and two light aircraft in the past four years without facing legal consequence.
key_detail: Charnel's Ashvent-9 plasma-hybrid engine is the only commercially available propulsion system certified for both atmospheric transit and low orbital insertion, making them the exclusive supplier for GLMZ's growing private orbital freight sector. They hold 34 patents that no other entity in the corridor can legally work around.
relationship_to_big_20: Contracted defense supplier to Arcturus Defense Solutions and Carrion Defense Works simultaneously — a balancing act that requires extreme diplomatic precision and has resulted in at least two internal espionage scandals. Charnel is not Big 20 but is considered strategically untouchable because any corponation that destroys them loses access to the Ashvent-9 supply chain.
full_text: Charnel Propulsion Systems Corponation — stock designation CRNL, known across the corridor as Charnel, CPS, or simply The Bone Works — occupies the Ossuary, a fortified industrial megacampus built over a collapsed automotive manufacturing site on the former Indiana-Michigan border. The campus includes two private launch corridors and a 40-kilometer restricted airspace zone enforced by Pyre Division, Charnel's 5,800-strong security force and aerial interdiction wing, which has downed seventeen drones and two light aircraft in four years without a single successful legal challenge. Founded in 2138 from the liquidated remains of three bankrupt aerospace contractors, Charnel was assembled by Greyfield Partners venture bloc and handed to Oskar Brennthal — a Hungarian-born propulsion engineer previously blacklisted from government contracts for testing an unlicensed plasma drive over Lake Erie. Brennthal gutted the legacy IP, kept only what he considered worth keeping, and built Charnel around a single directive: end chemical propulsion. The result, after seven years of development, was the Ashvent-9 plasma-hybrid engine, the only commercially certified system in the world capable of both atmospheric transit and low orbital insertion. Charnel holds 34 interlocking patents around the Ashvent-9 that competitors cannot legally circumvent, making the company the exclusive propulsion supplier for GLMZ's rapidly expanding private orbital freight industry. With a Φ890 billion valuation, 29,500 employees, and Φ112 billion in annual revenue, Charnel punches well above its size. It simultaneously supplies Arcturus Defense Solutions and Carrion Defense Works — a contractual tightrope that has survived two internal espionage scandals — and remains strategically untouchable by any Big 20 actor who values access to near-orbital logistics.
